subsystems.name: Quantum processor
subsystems.role: holds and manipulates qubits; today this means superconducting circuits at millikelvin temperatures or trapped ions.

subsystems.name: Cryogenic and control hardware
subsystems.role: keeps qubits cold and delivers precisely shaped microwave or laser pulses.

subsystems.name: Quantum–classical interface
subsystems.role: reads out qubit states and hands results to ordinary electronics fast enough to matter.

subsystems.name: Quantum sensing layer
subsystems.role: the most mature quantum contribution to robotics: cold-atom or atomic-vapour sensors for navigation, timing and magnetic fields.

subsystems.name: Robot platform
subsystems.role: the body that acts on the results — arms, wheels or legs, all classical.

subsystems.name: Hybrid software stack
subsystems.role: maps a robotics problem (task allocation, path planning, sampling) onto qubit operations and back.

buildSteps.title: Choose a task where quantum might actually help
buildSteps.detail: Combinatorial allocation, sampling or search problems are candidates; smooth control and perception usually are not, and classical chips win.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate or program the qubit layer
buildSteps.detail: Superconducting qubits are patterned on silicon wafers in a cleanroom; ion-trap designs instead load individual atoms and address them with lasers.

buildSteps.title: Cool, shield and wire the processor
buildSteps.detail: A dilution refrigerator takes the chip to around 10 millikelvin, with filtered cabling carrying signals down through several temperature stages.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate gates and readout
buildSteps.detail: Engineers tune pulse amplitudes and phases and measure error rates per gate, typically around one part in a thousand for the best two-qubit gates today.

buildSteps.title: Build the hybrid loop
buildSteps.detail: The processor returns samples or measurement outcomes; a classical computer updates the problem and sends the next circuit, within a latency budget set by the robot's motion.

buildSteps.title: Add quantum sensors
buildSteps.detail: Atomic inertial sensors or clocks are mounted to give drift-resistant navigation where satellite positioning is unavailable.

buildSteps.title: Integrate onto the robot with classical fallbacks
buildSteps.detail: The quantum unit sits in a rack or off-board and talks to the robot over a network; every safety-relevant decision still runs on certified classical hardware.

buildSteps.title: Benchmark against classical baselines
buildSteps.detail: Every claimed advantage must be measured against the best classical algorithm on the same task, at the same wall-clock time.

prerequisites.why: today's physical qubits fail often enough that thousands are needed to make one reliable logical qubit.
readout and feedback at microsecond timescales have been demonstrated in labs but are not a standard component.
a dilution refrigerator is room-sized and power-hungry, so nothing quantum-computing goes on a mobile robot yet.
atomic clocks, magnetometers and inertial sensors exist in commercial and lab forms, but are still bulky and costly.

prerequisites.tech: Quantum algorithms with proven robotics advantage
prerequisites.why: no published result yet shows a practical robot task solved faster or better end-to-end on quantum hardware.

pathway.milestone: quantum annealing and small gate-based processors used in research on optimisation and machine learning; quantum sensors used in laboratory navigation experiments
pathway.unlocks: a clearer map of which robotics problems are even candidates.

pathway.milestone: early error-corrected logical qubits, with processors kept in a rack and reached over a network by classical robots
pathway.unlocks: hybrid systems where the quantum part is a cloud-style accelerator rather than an on-board component.

pathway.milestone: ruggedised quantum sensor packages for positioning and timing on vehicles
pathway.unlocks: reliable navigation and coordination where satellite signals are jammed or absent — the most credible near-term robotics benefit.

pathway.milestone: on-board quantum co-processors in a portable package
pathway.unlocks: speculative: robots whose planning and control genuinely run on quantum hardware, if error correction and cryogenics shrink dramatically.
